_comment: Component library for the bee portrait system. Each slot holds written descriptions, not sprites. Isolated sprites do not sit on a head convincingly, because the light angle varies about 40 degrees across the shipped portraits and the contact shadow around a raised feature depends on what it is sitting on. So the model renders the whole head at once with these slots filled in. Grow each list toward 100 or beyond. The assembler does not care how many entries there are.
_slots_are_open: Add entries freely. Every entry needs an id and a phrase. The phrase is dropped word for word into the prompt, so write it the way you would describe the thing to somebody sculpting it. Test a new entry at small sizes, because anything that collapses into a shape the library already has at 24 to 48 pixels adds nothing.
_taken_by_note: The taken_by fields name the roster this library was built for (Honey, Fizz, Bumble, Hive, Comb, Nectar, Jelly). They are here so those bees keep their own components. Your roster is different, so --respect-taken will skip the wrong things for you. Either clear these fields or leave the flag off.

_hard_rules: Headwear is decorative. It may depict anything, personality, sports, occupation, whatever is fun, but it does not encode what the agent does. A bee in a cowboy hat is not a cowboy, it is a bee wearing a cowboy hat. Role lives in the antenna tip. That is what lets the headwear vocabulary stay open without competing with the tip.

The glasses slot is switched off in _disabled_slots. The 100 entries stay in the file, and the assembler skips the slot unless you pass an explicit --glasses identifier. Remove the slot from _disabled_slots to turn it on. It is off because glasses and eyes compete for the same small area.
Accessories are rare on purpose, about one bee in six. An accessory every bee has identifies nobody.

Base colours past the first ten were packed by clay_colours.py, which places new colours as far as it can from the ones already taken, measured in CIELAB inside the range where clay looks like clay. Before you commit a colour to a new roster bee, run clay_colours.py check on it. Colour is the axis people actually read at small sizes, and it runs out first, so a colour that merely looks different at full size may not be.
_disabled_slots_note: The glasses slot is filled with 100 entries but switched off by owner decision, because glasses compete with the eyes for the same space. Remove "glasses" from _disabled_slots to turn it on.
